dedupe_keys.name: fault tree encoding of the dhs resilience framework for robustness of gnss based pnt solutions

description: This conference paper investigates using fault trees as a formal system to encode the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) resilience framework for positioning, navigation and timing (PNT), so that the robustness of GNSS-based solutions in critical infrastructures can be assessed in a partly automated, repeatable way. It argues that resilience against signal disturbances is an important property of GNSS-based PNT, that failure to provide correct PNT information in critical domains may have a major societal impact, that solutions need regular reassessment over their lifetime, and that automation needs a machine-readable structure with well-established meaning. Producer: six authors, presented at the European Navigation Conference 2023 and published on 29 October 2023. Coverage: a generic method for PNT solutions in critical infrastructure. Access: open access; the abstract and licence were taken from the OpenAlex record because the publisher page refused the cloud session. Licence and cost: CC BY per OpenAlex, free to read. Caveats: the abstract describes an investigation of the encoding, and no software or worked results were read here. Simulation uses: fault trees give a structure for resilience and exposure analysis of positioning dependence in infrastructure systems. Related record: the European GNSS cross-sectoral disruption impacts case (case_study-europe-gnss-cross-sectoral-disruption-impacts).
